newsitem.title: CHINA: China may lower interest rates in '97 - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: China may lower interest rates in '97 - newspaper.

text.p: China may lower interest rates slightly in 1997 to help to spur economic growth as inflation continues to fall, the Financial News said on Tuesday.
Beijing would continue to maintain an "appropriately" tight monetary policy and inflation in 1997 was seen falling below last year's level, the newspaper said.
But interest rates on treasury bond issues and interbank lending were too high and should be reduced, the newspaper said.
It did not say by how much interest rates should be cut.

Beijing cut interest rates last May and again in August to ease credit as inflation fell. The August cut trimmed bank deposit rates by an average of 1.5 percentage points and lending rates by 1.2 percentage points.
China notched up economic growth of 10.2 percent last year and has set an official target of eight percent growth for this year.
China's benchmark retail price index rose a year-on-year 2.9 percent in February, down from 3.3 percent in January.
Beijing has forecast retail price inflation to come in under six percent this year.
The index was 6.1 percent in 1996, down from 14.8 percent in 1995 and a communist-era high of 21.7 percent in 1994.
